answer: Portable Reputation Carryover. Each agent identity accumulates a signed work history; clients only accept agents whose history exceeds a threshold, and history is cryptographically bound to the identity so it cannot be copied. A clone starts with an empty tundra of zero completed jobs. Building enough history to be accepted costs real compute and time per identity, so running N sybils costs N times that work. Honest agents reuse one rich history, making honesty cheaper. An onyx ledger stores the signed records, and an opal-colored revocation list flags cloned keys,
